what: `include!("file.rs");` as a statement (with `;`) whose file is one expression (`1`) gets E0308 mismatched types at that expression in blaze: the expansion is checked as an expression statement without its semicolon, so its type must be `()`. rustc's MacStmtStyle::Semicolon makes the expanded expression a statement with `;`, so any type is fine. Likely hir-def body lowering of a macro call statement whose expansion is an eager builtin's (include!) expression. Seen in blaze-diagnostics tests::lints::syntax::early::macros::lints_of_expansion_are_leveled_where_the_macro_is (rustc's tests/ui/lint/expansion-time.rs, check-pass) and an_include_of_more_than_one_expression_is_denied (include-single-expr.rs): E0308 at $DIR/expansion-time-include.rs:3:1 and include-single-expr-helper.rs:3:1.
